bullets: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's abrupt exit amid a China-spy probe roiled AI/semis Nov 12; shares pared losses but sector volatility stays elevated.
Hot CPI/PPI prints lifted Fed December hike odds to 100% (13% chance of 50bp); 10Y near 5.1%, 2Y up 15bp pressuring risk assets.
Asia rebounded (Nikkei +1.6%, Kospi +1.3%) and Europe edged higher; US futures recovered modestly (S&P +0.3%, Nasdaq +0.4%) after Thursday's selloff.
Core PPI m/m due today (est. 0.3%) after Tuesday's hot CPI; a hotter print would reinforce hawkish Fed bets and extend yield-driven pressure.

HRB.why: Q1 adjusted loss widened to -$1.40 (vs -$1.20) and opex rose 11% on the earnings report; Goldman maintained a Sell rating right after. Company-specific damage explains the drop, not sector or macro conditions that day.
HRB.bull: Revenue still grew 10%, management reaffirmed outlook and capital returns; selloff may be overdone for a seasonal business.
HRB.bear: Loss widened, expenses up 11%, and Goldman's Sell call targets HRB specifically, a fundamental not macro red flag.

EAT.why: Shares fell on unusually light volume (rvol 0.58) after a sharp rally faded; Wells Fargo trimmed its PT but kept Overweight. No guidance cut or miss found, and the Discretionary sector was actually higher that day.
EAT.bull: Ratings overwhelmingly buy (20/2/1), guidance raised last quarter, traffic-led momentum intact; looks like valuation-driven profit-taking.
EAT.bear: No clear catalyst found; a low-volume drift with no sector tailwind leaves the bounce thesis unconfirmed.

GDDY.why: Drop aligns with a broad Software/Tech selloff (sector -7% to -8%) amid the Nvidia-CEO shock and rate-hike fears, not fresh GDDY news. The securities lawsuit stems from an October disclosure; recent analyst PT revisions (Citi, UBS, Evercore) were upward.
GDDY.bull: Citigroup reiterated Buy, raising PT to $135; the lawsuit and bad news are already priced in from October.
GDDY.bear: An ongoing securities fraud class action over customer-acquisition disclosures remains an overhang if new facts surface.

DBX.why: DBX priced/upsized a $1.1B convertible note offering Nov 9-10, a dilutive financing event, and UBS downgraded to Sell (PT $26) the same week. This is company-specific balance-sheet news, a classic share-offering red flag.
DBX.bull: Notes fund a $175M buyback and term-loan paydown; RBC stayed Outperform (PT $48) after an earnings beat.
DBX.bear: Convertible dilution plus a fresh UBS Sell rating are company-specific negatives that fully explain the drop.

ISRG.why: Stock drifted down post-Q3 despite 22% revenue growth, pressured by a disclosed $450M antitrust settlement charge and a >53x valuation amid broader rate-driven de-risking of growth stocks; the Health sector itself was up that day.
ISRG.bull: Fundamentals are strong: 22% revenue growth, rising da Vinci 5/Ion adoption, ratings 26 buy vs 2 sell.
ISRG.bear: A disclosed $450M antitrust charge and stretched valuation are company-specific risks layered on top of macro de-risking.
